handbookNote: Kansas Driving Handbook (Non-Commercial Driver's Manual), Kansas Department of Revenue, Division of Vehicles -- AAMVA 09 Model Test Version, revised February 2022, fetched directly from the official ksrevenue.gov site (https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/dlhb.pdf, linked from https://www.ksrevenue.gov/dovteen.html and https://www.ksrevenue.gov/dovdrlic.html) and extracted from the official PDF with pdftotext (full text saved to temp/handbooks/ks/driver.txt, 4,959 lines / ~327KB). Real exam mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the manual's own Section 11 'Knowledge Test' text: the Kansas non-commercial knowledge test consists of 25 multiple-choice questions on traffic signs, pavement markings, and Kansas laws/driving practices; you must score 80% (20 of 25 correct) to pass; the test is explicitly stated to be 'not timed, but generally takes 15 to 20 minutes to finish'; and a failed applicant gets 4 total attempts before a mandatory 6-month wait. This is a large, detailed AAMVA-model manual (12 sections covering licensing/GDL, state traffic laws, fitness to drive, vehicle safety equipment, basic vehicle control, right-of-way, the full catalog of warning/regulatory/guide/incident signs and pavement markings, school bus and parking law, speed/space management with specific stopping-distance figures, collision avoidance and emergency procedures, sharing the road with pedestrians/bicyclists/motorcyclists/commercial vehicles/animal-drawn vehicles, rural/night/weather/work-zone driving, and the pre-trip vehicle safety inspection) that comfortably supports a large, non-repetitive question bank -- price matches this project's established Driver tier ($4.99), not a placeholder. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific, cited passage of the fetched official manual text (section and, where applicable, K.S.A. statute citation given in each question's source_note); none are invented, generic 'common knowledge', or reused from another state's numbers.
